subject: Feature fission & tier-bridging proposal for HealthCo renewal
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthco.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Meera Patel <meera.p@healthco.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options ahead of renewal

Hi Jonas,

We’re starting renewal planning for our early-2028 contract and want to explore a more modular packaging approach. Two asks from our side: 1) can we split a handful of high-value features into optional add-ons (feature-level billing) so we can trial them across different product teams, and 2) we need a clear upgrade/downgrade path with defined credits so teams can move between tiers without causing billing surprises.

Current constraints: multi-product rollout across 6 squads, predictable monthly spend for the finance team, and a hard renewal decision in December.

Can you provide 2–3 concrete pricing scenarios that show: modular add-on pricing, upgrade/downgrade credit mechanics, and an estimate of impact on average monthly spend? If there’s a short template you prefer (spreadsheet), send it over and we’ll fill usage samples.

Thanks — want to have this in time for our July procurement review.

—Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Partnerships, HealthCo
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthco.com>
Cc: Meera Patel <meera.p@healthco.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options ahead of renewal

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely do that. I’ve attached a starter workbook (HealthCo_MA_plan_v1.xlsx) that lays out a) three packaging scenarios, b) how upgrade/downgrade credits would flow, and c) estimated monthly impact given the usage profile you mentioned.

Looping in Ben for throughput and modal recommendations (hosted vs dedicated), and Marissa for packaging/credit structure. Lauren is on copy as a single-point escalation for any concession requests so approvals are fast.

Next steps: if you can drop a couple of sample usage slices into the sheet (or tell us which squads you want to pilot modular features), we’ll produce the formal 3-scenario pricing by EOD Friday. Also propose a 30-min workshop on Monday to walk the scenarios and agree on a preferred path.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Packaging options ahead of renewal

Jonas / Sanjay — quick notes on the capacity and SKU side that will affect the pricing scenarios:

- If HealthCo wants feature-level add-ons that are inference-heavy (summarization, reranking), we should model both seat-based and token/throughput metering. The dominant driver will be peak concurrency for the squads that enable the feature.
- Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) let us offer tighter per-token pricing and predictable latency; good candidate for top-tier customers or squads with steady usage.
- Hosted (metered) is cheaper to start and gives flexibility for trial squads, but upgrade/downgrade credits need a simple conversion (we typically convert committed-GPU credits to per-token equivalents at the 30-day average rate).

Proposed quick conversion rule for the scenarios: 1 reserved GPU-month = 6M token-units (example), and we offer pro-rated credit when moving from Reserved -> Hosted or between Reserved sizes. For downgrade protection, offer a one-time migration credit equal to unused committed months * 0.6 as dollar credit applied to Hosted invoice.

I’ll push some numbers into the workbook (scenario tabs) — rough placeholders for now.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthco.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bennett <lauren.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options ahead of renewal

Thanks — I’ve drafted three discrete packaging options and attached a PDF summarizing the tradeoffs (modular_pricing_3_scenarios.pdf). TL;DR:

1) Modular Pilot (low friction): Core tier unchanged, 3 optional feature add-ons priced per-seat/month with a small per-token surcharge for heavy inference. No long-term commit; ideal for trialing across squads.

2) Hybrid Commit (mid): Core tier + selected add-ons bundled into a mid-commit plan. 12-month commitment with step-down protection (credits applied pro-rata). We propose a 10% bundle discount if 3+ squads adopt within 90 days.

3) Dedicated Bridge (enterprise): Reserved capacity for mission-critical squads, add-ons mapped to reserved throughput buckets. Upgrade/downgrade policy: 30-day notice, pro-rated credit, and a one-time migration credit for net-new reserved purchases. Includes 90-day price protection for teams moved into Dedicated during the renewal window.

Concessions guidance: for HealthCo (deal HLT-4921), we can offer a one-time onboarding credit up to $25k if they commit to scenario 2 or 3 by 2027-12-31 (needs Lauren’s sign-off for exceptions > $15k). Lauren — can you confirm approval threshold and if we can pre-approve a $25k credit?

Sanjay — if you want, we can include a sample 6-month rollout plan by squad that shows cost delta per scenario. If you share the usage slices in the workbook, I’ll finalize the scenario numbers.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Packaging, Redwood Inference
Attachments: modular_pricing_3_scenarios.pdf
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@healthco.com>

Appreciate the fast turnaround, team. Monday workshop works for us — Meera will drop sample usage slices into the workbook by EOD tomorrow.

We’d like to aim for Scenario 2 as a preferred path but want to see the exact $/month deltas and the credit math before we take it to procurement. Also agree on the need for clear downgrade protection.

Invite the workshop for Monday 10:00am PT if that fits your calendar.

—Sanjay
Head of Platform Partnerships, HealthCo
